Washington), carefully and answer the questions based on it. The excerpt calls for the nonviolent struggle against racial segregation, urging the use of moral means — never violence or hatred — and stressing that the goal of the struggle is justice for all, not the humiliation of the oppressor.

1. Give two pieces of advice the author gives to those fighting for freedom. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 1. **(1)** Always struggle using moral means and moral weapons, never resorting to violence. **(2)** Move with dignity and discipline, using only the weapon of love, without becoming bitter or hateful.

**Section C: Reading Comprehension (10 marks).** Read the following excerpt from Martin Luther King Jr.'s writings, "A Testament of Hope" (source: *The Essential Writings of Martin Luther King Jr.*, edited by James M. Washington), carefully and answer the questions based on it. The excerpt calls for the nonviolent struggle against racial segregation, urging the use of moral means — never violence or hatred — and stressing that the goal of the struggle is justice for all, not the humiliation of the oppressor.

2. According to the passage, what is the effect of using violence in one's struggle? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown: 2. **Violence leaves future/unborn generations to inherit a long and desolate night of bitterness**, its chief legacy being an endless reign of meaningless chaos rather than genuine freedom.

questions.corrige_markdown: 3. **Many Negroes who devote their lives to the cause of freedom, together with many white people of good will and strong moral sensitivity** who are willing to take a stand for justice.

6. Identify four things which freedom fighters should make their enemies understand, according to the passage. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 6. **(1)** That they are not seeking to defeat or humiliate the oppressor. **(2)** That they are not seeking revenge for past injustices. **(3)** That they are seeking justice for the oppressor just as much as for themselves. **(4)** That the "sore" of segregation wounds the oppressor just as much as it wounds the oppressed.
